what_its_for: Toremifene is used to treat breast cancer in women who have gone through menopause. It works by blocking estrogen (a female hormone) in the body, which helps slow down or stop the growth of certain types of breast cancer cells that need estrogen to grow.
how_to_take: Take toremifene by mouth with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food. Try to take it at the same time every day to help you remember. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush or chew it.
dosing: The usual dose is one 60 mg tablet taken once a day. Always follow your doctor's instructions exactly. Do not change your dose on your own without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store toremifene tablets at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep the tablets away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Store in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medication after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice while taking this medicine, as it can increase the amount of drug in your blood and raise the risk of side effects. Tell your doctor about ALL medications you take, including over-the-counter drugs and supplements, because many medicines can interact with toremifene. Avoid starting any new medications without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first. Do not take toremifene if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it can harm an unborn baby.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: chest pain, fast or irregular heartbeat, shortness of breath, sudden dizziness or fainting, severe leg pain or swelling (possible blood clot), sudden vision changes, unusual vaginal bleeding, yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice), severe nausea or vomiting, or signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing. Also call your doctor if you feel unusually tired, confused, or if your symptoms do not seem to be improving.
when_it_works: Toremifene starts working in your body right away after you take it, but you may not notice changes in your cancer symptoms for several weeks or even months. It is important to keep taking this medicine every day, even if you feel well. Your doctor will check your progress with regular appointments and tests to see how the treatment is working.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Toremifene must NOT be used during pregnancy. It can cause serious harm to an unborn baby. Use effective birth control while taking this medicine and talk to your doctor right away if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while taking toremifene, as it may pass into breast milk and harm a nursing baby. Older adults: Older patients generally use the same dose, but should be monitored closely for side effects such as dizziness and heart rhythm changes. Liver problems: If you have liver disease, tell your doctor before starting this medicine, as toremifene may not be safe for you or your dose may need to be adjusted. Heart conditions: Tell your doctor if you have a history of irregular heartbeat (QT prolongation), heart failure, or low potassium or magnesium levels, as toremifene can affect heart rhythm.
